correctness.rationale: If the structure matrix is invertible, the algebra is perfect and hence semiprime. If it has rank one under full support, A^2 is one-dimensional and every nonzero ideal contains A^2. Thus semiprimeness is equivalent to (A^2)^2 being nonzero. Writing e2^2=(b/a)e1^2 gives (e1^2)^2=((a^3+b c^2)/a)e1^2, proving the defect equation. The complete graph is downward directed, so the inspected primeness theorem makes semiprime equivalent to prime. The packaged checker independently enumerates ideals and ideal products for q=2,3,5,7.

value.rationale: The motivating paper's main negative result says the graph cannot decide semiprimeness and illustrates this with one pair. The accepted theorem determines the entire smallest full-support graph fiber, sharply separating perfect, semiprime-nonperfect, and nonsemiprime regions. The rank-one semiprime stratum shows that nonperfection is usually not the obstruction: over F_q, only a 1/(q-1) fraction of the nonperfect full-support matrices fail semiprimeness.
